statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clearing p16(Ink4a)-positive cells with AP20187 lengthened median lifespan in male and female mice from two distinct genetic backgrounds.
statements.evidence: AP20187 treatment extended median lifespan in both male and female mice of two distinct genetic backgrounds
statements.note: The study reports AP20187-induced clearance extended median lifespan in both sexes across two genetic backgrounds.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Clearing senescent cells improved memory and cognitive performance in the aged mice.
statements.evidence: including kidney, heart and fat, where clearance preserved the functionality of glomeruli, cardio-protective KATP channels and adipocytes, respectively
statements.note: The organs assessed were kidney, heart and fat; brain function or cognition was not examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Removing p16(Ink4a)-positive cells delayed tumour formation and curbed age-related deterioration of kidney, heart and fat without apparent side effects.
statements.evidence: The clearance of p16(Ink4a)-positive cells delayed tumorigenesis and attenuated age-related deterioration of several organs without apparent side effects
statements.note: Clearance both delayed tumorigenesis and attenuated organ deterioration with no apparent side effects.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Naturally accumulating p16(Ink4a)-positive cells shorten lifespan and drive age-dependent changes across several organs.
statements.evidence: p16(Ink4a)-positive cells that accumulate during adulthood negatively influence lifespan and promote age-dependent changes in several organs
statements.note: The conclusion attributes shortened lifespan and organ changes to accumulated p16-positive cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Dasatinib plus quercetin lowered the number of naturally occurring senescent cells and their proinflammatory cytokine secretion in human adipose tissue explants.
statements.evidence: decreased the number of naturally occurring senescent cells and their secretion of frailty-related proinflammatory cytokines in explants of human adipose tissue
statements.note: The senolytic cocktail decreased senescent cell numbers and their cytokine secretion in human fat explants.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In mice, intermittent oral senolytics raised post-treatment survival by 36% and cut the mortality hazard to 65%.
statements.evidence: increased post-treatment survival by 36% while reducing mortality hazard to 65%
statements.note: Oral senolytics increased post-treatment survival by 36% and reduced the mortality hazard to 65%.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Transplanting senescent cells into young mice impaired their cognitive performance.
statements.evidence: transplanting relatively small numbers of senescent cells into young mice is sufficient to cause persistent physical dysfunction, as well as to spread cellular senescence to host tissues
statements.note: The study measured physical dysfunction and senescence spread, not cognition.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transplanting even fewer senescent cells into older recipient mice produced the same dysfunction and was accompanied by reduced survival.
statements.evidence: Transplanting even fewer senescent cells had the same effect in older recipients and was accompanied by reduced survival
statements.note: Fewer transplanted senescent cells had the same effect in older mice, with reduced survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Early genetic ablation of senescent cells improved pulmonary function and physical health, though lung fibrosis itself appeared unchanged.
statements.evidence: early-intervention suicide-gene-mediated senescent cell ablation improves pulmonary function and physical health, although lung fibrosis is visibly unaltered
statements.note: Ablating senescent cells improved function and health while fibrosis was visibly unaltered.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Dasatinib plus quercetin improved lung function in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
statements.evidence: DQ treatment replicates benefits of transgenic clearance
statements.note: DQ benefits were demonstrated in the mouse model; no treatment of patients is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Senescence biomarkers were more abundant in IPF lung, and p16 expression rose with increasing disease severity.
statements.evidence: elevated abundance of senescence biomarkers in IPF lung, with p16 expression increasing with disease severity
statements.note: The study found higher senescence biomarkers and p16 rising with disease severity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The secretome of senescent fibroblasts, selectively killed by dasatinib plus quercetin, was fibrogenic.
statements.evidence: the secretome of senescent fibroblasts, which are selectively killed by a senolytic cocktail, dasatinib plus quercetin (DQ), is fibrogenic
statements.note: The senescent fibroblast secretome was shown to be fibrogenic.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: TET2-deficient macrophages secreted more interleukin-1β through the NLRP3 inflammasome.
statements.evidence: TET2-deficient macrophages exhibited an increase in NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated interleukin-1β secretion
statements.note: TET2-deficient macrophages showed increased NLRP3-mediated IL-1β secretion.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Partial reconstitution with TET2-deficient bone marrow cells drove their clonal expansion and markedly enlarged atherosclerotic plaques.
statements.evidence: partial bone marrow reconstitution with TET2-deficient cells was sufficient for their clonal expansion and led to a marked increase in atherosclerotic plaque size
statements.note: TET2-deficient cells expanded clonally and markedly increased plaque size.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Expansion of TET2-mutant blood cells increased the risk of leukemia in the mice.
statements.evidence: Several of these recurrent mutations, including those in the gene encoding the epigenetic modifier enzyme TET2, promote expansion of the mutant blood cells
statements.note: The study examined atherosclerosis; blood-cancer outcomes were not assessed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: An NLRP3 inhibitor was more atheroprotective in mice carrying TET2-deficient cells than in nonchimeric mice.
statements.evidence: An NLRP3 inhibitor showed greater atheroprotective activity in chimeric mice reconstituted with TET2-deficient cells than in nonchimeric mice
statements.note: The inhibitor protected TET2-chimeric mice more than nonchimeric mice.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Eliminating senescent cells also reduced joint damage in rheumatoid arthritis.
statements.evidence: Collectively, these findings support the use of SnCs as a therapeutic target for treating degenerative joint disease
statements.note: The study concerns post-traumatic and degenerative osteoarthritis; rheumatoid arthritis is never addressed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clearing senescent cells from cultured OA-patient chondrocytes lowered senescent and inflammatory markers while raising cartilage extracellular-matrix proteins.
statements.evidence: decreased expression of senescent and inflammatory markers while also increasing expression of cartilage tissue extracellular matrix proteins
statements.note: Removal lowered senescence and inflammation markers and raised matrix protein expression in patient chondrocytes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: An intra-articular senolytic injection reproduced these benefits in transgenic, non-transgenic and aged mice.
statements.evidence: Intra-articular injection of a senolytic molecule that selectively killed SnCs validated these results in transgenic, non-transgenic and aged mice
statements.note: The injected senolytic validated the findings across three mouse groups.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Selectively eliminating senescent cells after ACLT limited post-traumatic osteoarthritis, reduced pain, and increased cartilage development.
statements.evidence: selective elimination of these cells attenuated the development of post-traumatic OA, reduced pain and increased cartilage development
statements.note: Clearing senescent cells attenuated OA, lowered pain, and increased cartilage development.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the MAPT P301S PS19 tau-disease model, p16-positive senescent astrocytes and microglia accumulated.
statements.evidence: accumulates p16 INK4A -positive senescent astrocytes and microglia
statements.note: The tau model accumulated p16-positive senescent astrocytes and microglia.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clearing senescent cells as they arose prevented gliosis, tau hyperphosphorylation, tangle deposition and the loss of cortical and hippocampal neurons, preserving cognition.
statements.evidence: Clearance of these cells as they arise using INK-ATTAC transgenic mice prevents gliosis, hyperphosphorylation of both soluble and insoluble tau leading to neurofibrillary tangle deposition, and degeneration of cortical and hippocampal neurons, thus preserving cognitive function
statements.note: Senescent cell clearance blocked tau pathology and neuron degeneration while preserving cognition.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.evidence: Collectively, these results show that senescent cells have a role in the initiation and progression of tau-mediated disease, and suggest that targeting senescent cells may provide a therapeutic avenue for the treatment of these pathologies
statements.note: The work concerns tau pathology; amyloid-beta is never mentioned or measured.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A first-generation senolytic drug altered tau aggregation.
statements.evidence: Pharmacological intervention with a first-generation senolytic modulates tau aggregation
statements.note: Pharmacological senolytic treatment modulated tau aggregation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting p62 specifically in macrophages caused marked buildup of damaged mitochondria and excessive IL-1β-driven inflammation, increasing macrophage death.
statements.evidence: Macrophage-specific p62 ablation causes pronounced accumulation of damaged mitochondria and excessive IL-1β-dependent inflammation, enhancing macrophage death
statements.note: p62 ablation increased damaged-mitochondria accumulation, IL-1β inflammation and macrophage death.

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cytosolic oxidized mtDNA binds the NLRP3 inflammasome complex and is required for its activation.
